newsitem.title: USA: U.S. consumer group seeks open meeting on heat oil.
newsitem.headline: U.S. consumer group seeks open meeting on heat oil.

text.p: A U.S. consumer group on Thursday urged Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary to allow the public to attend a meeting she had scheduled with oil industry executives next week.

But an Energy Department spokesman said the October 18 meeting would remain closed to all but a group of about 20 industry leaders involved in supply, distribution, marketing and consumption of winter heating fuels, Energy Department spokesman Bill Wicker said.

"I find it outrageous that the Department of Energy would even consider such a closed-door meeting in light of the many concerns that have been expressed regarding the huge run-up in prices for both diesel and heating oil as well as efforts by major oil refiners to maintain excessively low middle distillate inventories," Citizen Action's energy director Edwin Rothschild said in an October 10 letter to O'Leary.
While O'Leary held public meetings sometimes, Wicker said in this case "a public meeting might be counterproductive".

"She will be most interested in learning (the industry's) perspectives on factors affecting the availability and price volatility of winter heating fuels, ... and discuss steps the government should be prepared to take to address these circumstances," he said.
Rothschild attacked the Energy Department for showing a lack of concern to consumers. However Wicker said: "We're aware and we're monitoring, but we're not panicked."
